newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Eastern to benefit from single fare.
newsitem.headline: China Eastern to benefit from single fare.

text.p: China Eastern Airlines Corp Ltd will benefit from the Chinese government's intention to unify international and domestic air fares, its president Li Zhongming said on Tuesday.

International passengers paid about 20 percent more than domestic passengers, he said, adding it was expected the government would increase domestic fares by about 10 percent, while international fares would be cut by about 10 percent.
"We believe our revenues will rise after the unification of fares," he told a news conference at which the company presented its 1996 earnings results,
China Eastern reported net profit of HK$590.64 million yuan in 1996. This was the company's first annual results report since listing, and no comparative figures were given.
Li said the single fare system would be implemented in July, but he gave no further details.
Passenger traffic accounted for about 81 percent of China Eastern's total revenues in 1996 and the Shanghai-based airliner carried more domestic than international passengers.
Li said the airline's total capacity rose 17.5 percent in the first quarter of 1997 from a year earlier and traffic by 10.5 percent.
But due to the large increase in capacity, the load factor declined by 6.0 percent to 51.4 percent in the first three months.
"The first quarter normally is a quiet season in China and we believe our revenues in the peak season from April to November will increase greatly," he said.
The airline planned to expand its fleet by buying five Airbus A-340 aircraft and nine McDonnell Douglas MD-90s over the coming four years using finance leasing, the company said in a statement.
It had 42 aircraft at the end of 1996, including 41 passenger planes and one MD-11F cargo aircraft.
